root_cause.text: In the ICSSG PRU Ethernet RX path, `emac_run_xdp()` stopped recycling pages on `XDP_DROP`, but the non-zero-copy `emac_rx_packet()` caller did not reclaim the `page_pool` page when `ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED` was returned, so dropped packets leaked pages instead of returning them to the pool.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (*xdp_state == ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED) { page_pool_recycle_direct(pool, page); goto requeue; }` in `emac_rx_packet()`, and the commit message explicitly says “Page recycling was removed from the XDP_DROP path in emac_run_xdp() … However, this causes a memory leak when running XDP programs that drop packets in non-zero-copy mode … The pages are never returned to the page pool.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (*xdp_state == ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED) { page_pool_recycle_direct(pool, page); goto requeue; }` in `emac_rx_packet()`, and the commit message explicitly says “Page recycling was removed from the XDP_DROP path in emac_run_xdp() … However, this causes a memory leak when running XDP programs that drop packets in non-zero-copy mode … The pages are never returned to the page pool.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle XDP-consumed packets by recycling the page immediately and skipping further RX processing.
intent_record.what: In `emac_rx_packet()`, after calling `emac_run_xdp()`, a new check was added for `*xdp_state == ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED`; in that case the code now calls `page_pool_recycle_direct(pool, page)` and jumps to `requeue` before the existing `*xdp_state != ICSSG_XDP_PASS` check.
intent_record.how: This makes XDP frames marked as consumed be immediately recycled back to the page pool and not proceed through the normal pass/redirect path, preventing the packet buffer from being reused incorrectly or leaked after XDP has taken ownership of it.

grouping_result.intent: Handle XDP-consumed packets by recycling the page immediately and skipping further RX processing.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it ensures XDP-consumed packets are recycled immediately, fixing the missing page_pool reclaim path that caused page leaks on dropped packets.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix condition only requeued non-PASS XDP outcomes, but the caller did not properly reclaim the page when XDP consumed the packet, allowing dropped/consumed packets to bypass page recycling and leak page_pool pages.

This jump was the only handling for non-PASS XDP results in the pre-fix code path, but it did not itself ensure the page was returned for ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED, which is the core leak described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix branch treated all non-PASS XDP outcomes the same by diverting to the requeue path, but it did not itself ensure the page was reclaimed for ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED. That allowed XDP_DROP/consumed packets in the RX path to bypass proper page_pool recycling and leak pages.

This was the only action taken for non-PASS XDP results in the vulnerable code path. Because the non-zero-copy caller did not reclaim the page when ICSSG_XDP_CONSUMED was returned, this jump failed to guarantee page return to the page_pool, enabling the leak described in the root cause.
